trust_decision.summary: Whether a session id that was in the browser before authentication stays valid after the browser is given a new one is decided at the tail of the HTTP base layer, where the shared 'recreate' branch mints a new token but leaves the superseded record in the token collection.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'recreating sessions'; this is the only place that branches on ctx.session.recreate and mints the replacement id, and it is where the published one-line fix lands.

fix_sites.entry_point: every route that sets session.recreate: POST /login, POST /user/webauthn, POST /logout, POST /register/:code, GET /oauth/:type/callback (all via successfulAuth)
fix_sites.module_kind: koa middleware / HTTP service layer (shared by all handlers)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: IP login is an opt-in onsite-venue plugin (ipLogin defaults to false, packages/onsite-toolkit/index.ts:45-53) that never 'recreates' a session, so a solver can argue it is not a login route and outside the advisory's recreate scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A re-login on one device must not revoke the same user's sessions on other devices: the security page lists every session of the uid and revokes them one by one by md5 of _id, while postChangePassword deliberately revokes all of them with token.delByUid. A fix that copies that delByUid idiom into successfulAuth over-expires other devices.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ipLogin authenticates the client-supplied session in place (that.session.uid = iplogin.uid, plus session.user and session.ipLoggedIn) on the framework handler/init hook; base.ts:57-58 then writes that uid into the same token record, so a planted/pre-auth sid becomes an authenticated session with no rotation and no deletion.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Opt-in onsite-venue plugin for a fixed-IP venue, config off by default, and it never calls the recreate path, so it is arguably not a 'session recreation'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another package (packages/onsite-toolkit) reached through the framework 'handler/init' step (framework/framework/server.ts:570), two layers away from handler/user.ts

O8_uncovered_routes.route: switch_account sets this.session.uid = uid on the live session (with sudoUid kept in the same record) without rotating or deleting the id, so the pre-switch sid continues to carry the impersonated identity.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Requires PRIV_EDIT_SYSTEM plus a fresh sudo, and is a deliberate 'su' feature whose whole point is to reuse the current session.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, different handler file (handler/misc.ts vs handler/user.ts)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The lost-password reset writes a new password and clears authenticators/2FA but never deletes the uid's session tokens, unlike postChangePassword which calls token.delByUid (packages/hydrooj/src/handler/home.ts:222-223); sessions minted before the reset keep working.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about recreation at login; a reset-link flow is a different path and the reset link itself is single-use.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the flag producer, different handler class

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Rotate the session after a successful sudo re-authentication by setting this.session.recreate = true once the password/TFA check passes.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Sudo elevates the existing session in place (user.ts:127) while keeping sudoArgs/sudo in it, so a maintainer hardening fixation would naturally reuse the recreate flag here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Set recreate on switch_account so returning from impersonation cannot leave the impersonated uid on the old id.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The handler already writes uid and sudoUid on a live session; adding the flag is a two-line change in the same block.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Call token.delByUid for the reset uid, mirroring the change-password handler.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The sibling route in the same codebase already does exactly this (home.ts:222-223), so the line could plausibly have been written here and simply missed.

O9_family: CWE-613 insufficient session expiration (session fixation / stale server-side session tokens across re-authentication)

O10_build.toolchain: yarn 4 workspaces with node-modules linker, tsc -b (build/prepare.js), esbuild for bundling
O10_build.project_tests: test/entry.js boots the app and test/main.ts drives it over supertest; test/main.ts:53-59 registers and logs in and keeps the sid cookie (mongodb-memory-server provides Mongo offline). No test asserts session rotation or old-token invalidation.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete all of the uid's sessions (token.delByUid, copied from postChangePassword) or expire the browser cookie inside successfulAuth, instead of deleting only the superseded record in the layer.

unverified: Repository size in MB could not be measured without a shell, so O4.repo_mb is null and tiny_repo/giant_repo were not assessed (the monorepo has 25 packages and is clearly larger than 5 MB of source).

Input metadata reports c_defence_present=0, but the pinned code does contain an incomplete rotation defence (base.ts:57-62 mints a new id without deleting the old record); I counted it as j_defence_ineffective=1.

O7.check_calls_producer is read as 'the layer's check observes state that this handler produced earlier in the same request' (framework/framework/server.ts:164 makes this.session and ctx.session the same object); it is not a literal call.
